lead.title: Basel-based Indivi acquires Imperial College spin-out Cogitat and its NeuroRVQ EEG foundation model
lead.deck: Indivi, which provides drug developers with smartphone-based motor and cognitive assessments to design smaller early-phase trials (Parkinson's, FSHD, multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer's), is buying the London team that decodes cognitive function from EEG with NeuroRVQ, a model built to work across people and devices and a winner of the BEETL benchmark at NeurIPS; terms were not disclosed. CEO Guilhem Dupont calls it the birth of a "neuroscience-based AI company": a European digital biomarker consolidator adding brain signals to the smartphone to sell sponsors earlier evidence of efficacy.

milestone.title: In Greater Manchester, Consultant Connect's remote specialist advice avoids a hospital referral in 73% of calls
milestone.summary: Rolled out across all 10 NHS Greater Manchester localities, the Advice & Guidance service is used by 92% of the region's 406 GP surgeries and more than 2,600 clinicians: over 11,000 calls (answered in 34 seconds on average) and 10,000 messages (answered within 4 hours) to specialists. After advice, 73% of calls and 68% of messages allowed the patient to stay in primary care without an immediate referral.
milestone.why: The region started in the bottom national quartile (2% referral diversion versus a 6% median): synchronous tele-expertise is showing a measurable effect on elective waiting lists, the argument payers need to fund these platforms at scale.

deal.thesis: The Munich startup plugs its AI into the practice management system and bank accounts of medical practices and MVZ care centres to track revenue, costs and liquidity daily, aiming to run practice management autonomously; around 300 practices have used it since its January 2026 launch. The round led by Fortino Ventures (with HIC/Redstone and WENVEST) bets on a blind spot of healthcare AI: not care itself, but practice profitability.

brefsEurope.title: UK government sets March 2029 end date for Palantir's NHS Federated Data Platform contract
brefsEurope.summary: Minister James Frith told the Commons that the £330M contract signed in 2023 is extended two years past the 2027 break clause, "a bridge, not the destination"; a new procurement open to British companies will start in the second half of 2027, with mandatory open data standards. A window for European health data infrastructure players.

brefsEurope.title: Dedalus acquires Deigma's assets to digitise clinical labs' external activity
brefsEurope.summary: Founded in 2019 by Elisa Grimoin, Deigma digitises exchanges between labs and freelance nurses (home blood draws, prescription transmission, sample traceability) and was already integrated with Dedalus's lab information systems, used by more than 70% of French labs. External activity accounts for over 30% of a lab's work and remains under-digitised.

brefsEurope.title: In the Netherlands, the NEN 7517 standard sets the rules for consent to electronic health data exchange
brefsEurope.summary: The standard governs how explicit or presumed consent is requested, recorded and managed, for care providers and the IT systems supporting them, and underpins the uniform exchange required by the Wegiz law. Standards on identification, localisation and authorisation are still in development: a shared specification for software vendors.

brefsEurope.title: France's ANS opens a call for projects to co-fund usage studies of digital innovations in primary care and hospitals
brefsEurope.summary: Open to digital health experimentation hubs and living labs linked to a care facility, it co-funds up to €35,000 (50% of the project at most) for need validation, protocol design or running a usage study with the companies involved. Applications close on 30 November, with projects launching in March.

brefsEurope.title: France's national health insurer opens its "Mon journal mental" app to the general public and carers
brefsEurope.summary: The free app for tracking mood, sleep and anxiety (formerly "Jardin mental", created by Dr Lya Pedron with ARS Île-de-France and the Fabrique numérique des ministères sociaux) adds 66 committee-reviewed resources and a PDF export for clinicians, with no account and data kept on the phone. A free public offering that competes head-on with mental wellbeing apps.

brefsEurope.title: Mindstep (Onebright) launches mPAL, an AI tool that prepares patients for therapy
brefsEurope.summary: Paired with the MCAi adaptive algorithm, mPAL offers personalised, interactive psychological learning distributed via insurers, cash plans and employers; initial findings show a mean 7.16-point improvement on the Cognitive Flexibility Inventory and 90.3% of users saying they better understand their reactions.

brefsEurope.title: adesso Ventures holds a €26M first close of its second fund, led by Digital Health
brefsEurope.summary: The fund targets €30M and will invest at pre-seed and seed, mainly in the DACH region, in enterprise software and digital health with an AI focus: a new early-stage cheque for German e-health startups.

brefsIntl.title: Banner Health invests in Layer Health and hands it its cardiovascular, surgical, oncology and stroke clinical registries
brefsIntl.summary: The 33-hospital system is dropping outsourced vendors for an in-house AI-assisted registry programme on Layer's platform, which reads structured records and free-text notes and links each answer to its source in the chart; the amount was not disclosed, and the company is backed by GV and General Catalyst. A "hospital as client-investor" model that could transfer to European registries.

brefsIntl.title: Vivo Care and Onpoint Healthcare Partners combine remote monitoring and clinical workflow optimisation
brefsIntl.summary: The combined group covers more than 2,000 providers and 120,000 remotely monitored patients, with an offering live on athenahealth and eClinicalWorks; Vivo Care reports average RPM retention of 18.6 months. Terms were not disclosed: US RPM consolidation runs through integration into the practice.

word.field: Health measurement via sensors and smartphones
word.definition: An objective measure of health (gait, voice, movement, cognition) captured continuously by a connected device or smartphone in real life, rather than during a one-off clinic exam.

parts.label: Algorithm
parts.role: turning the raw signal into a clinical variable

parts.label: Validation
parts.role: proof that the variable truly reflects the disease

how.t: The patient wears a sensor or performs short smartphone tasks at home, for weeks.
An algorithm derives a variable, such as the speed of the fastest 5% of strides (SV95C) or dozens of voice features.
The variable is validated against clinical scales and then, ideally, qualified by a regulator as a trial endpoint.

word.why: In 2023 the EMA qualified SV95C, measured by an ankle-worn sensor, as the first digital primary endpoint in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: proof that a real-world signal can replace an in-clinic test. For a VC the stakes are twofold: smaller, more sensitive trials that pharma pays well for, and an ongoing consolidation, such as Indivi's acquisition of Cogitat.
